---
title: "iv-image"
---

The IV provisioning layer for exe.dev VMs: a script (`provision-iv.sh`) plus
vendored skills and doc-site tooling that turn a stock `boldsoftware/exeuntu`
VM into an IV dev box.

## Why a script, not a custom image

- **Keep Shelley working.** A custom Docker image is not recognized by exe.dev
  as "exeuntu", which silently disables Shelley (exe.dev's built-in coding
  agent): no VMs-list icon, no detail-page Shelley button, and exe.dev never
  injects the shelley binary at VM creation. Stock exeuntu keeps Shelley fully
  working (icon, button, `https://<vm>.shelley.exe.xyz`).
- **Preinstall.** Provisioning bakes in DuckDB, Quarto, doc-site tooling, agent
  config, and team skills in one ~23-second pass onto stock exeuntu.
- **Reproducible compute for GitLake.** The custom image's only real advantage
  was reproducibility via pinned image digests; that is replaced by the
  recipe-pinning model below (git tag/sha + pinned tools + vendored skills,
  with the base exeuntu recorded in a lockfile).

## Layout

| File               | Role                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provision-iv.sh`  | Provisions the IV layer onto stock exeuntu (DuckDB + Quarto + agent config + skills); writes `~/iv-provision.lock`. |
| `vendor-skills.sh` | Refreshes the vendored skills snapshot in `skills/` (needs node/npx).   |
| `skills/`          | Vendored, pinned team skills — committed to the repo so they are frozen. |
| `bin/`             | `render-site` + `provision-docsite` + `gen-llms-txt` — installed onto PATH. |

## Reproducibility (recipe pinning)

The pinned artifact is the git commit of this repo: check out a specific tag/sha
on the VM, run `provision-iv.sh`, and you get the same result.

- Tool release versions and per-architecture checksums are pinned inside
  `provision-iv.sh`; re-running it repairs or upgrades mismatched versions.
- Skills are vendored into `skills/` (committed = frozen); `provision-iv.sh`
  copies them in with no node/npx needed on the VM.
- The base exeuntu image **cannot** be pinned — exe.dev manages it (floating)
  and there is no version/digest selector on `ssh exe.dev new`. Pinning it to a
  custom registry digest is exactly what breaks Shelley. Instead,
  `provision-iv.sh` records it in `~/iv-provision.lock` (exeuntu image revision,
  Shelley version, installed DuckDB/Quarto/AWS/Tigris/rclone/herdr versions,
  skills count, manifest pin, and provisioning Git SHA).

## Versioning

Versioning is via **Git tags of this provisioning repo**, not
`iv-image:MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Docker image tags. Pin a recipe by checking out a
tag/sha before running `provision-iv.sh`.

### Provisioning-era releases

| Version | Change |
| ------- | ------ |
| `2.6.0` | + `herdr` baked (0.7.4, pinned; SHA-256s computed locally — upstream ships no checksums). |
| `2.5.1` | upgrade-vm skill: mint Tailscale API access from the OAuth client instead of the revoked static API key (doc-only). |
| `2.5.0` | First hardened provisioning release: vendored skills, verified tool downloads, repairable version pins, safer SSH/Tailscale workflows, tests/CI, nginx doc serving, and Markdown/LLM doc artifacts. |
